verified: The opt-in local application supervisor verifies the pinned Collector hash and generated configuration, starts it on the validated loopback OTLP port before starting the API, and waits until the receiver accepts connections.
A real local PAPER API request returns a trace ID that is present in the retained Collector JSON file.
Collector configuration and trace-file path are retained under the local app state root; only the backend receives the trace-file path.
The owned Collector, API and UI process handles are terminal after supervisor cleanup, and the Collector listener port is released.
Native Collector acceptance continues to verify actual SDK export, protected trace reads, outage, restart and retained-file behavior.
Ruff lint and format checks pass for the changed Python files.
limitations: Managed Collector startup is opt-in and currently requires the pinned Windows native binary. Linux and service-manager deployment were not tested.
The local OTLP receiver has no authentication. Other processes able to access loopback can submit forged spans or consume receiver resources.
Trace files are local observations, not an audit journal or tamper-proof record. Metrics/log correlation, independent security review and all P00-P13 gates remain open.
